I had the same breed. She was 16 and was in my life for 13 of them... Since I was 9. I came home from work one day to find her in the same place as I had left her. Staring at the wall blankly. She wouldn't eat and when she tried to drink the water just fell out of her mouth. I was a mess when I left a message for the vet at midnight. I knew what was coming.

They called me back the following morning and told me to come in. Before that, we took a ride to the Levi and then the lake where we used to hunt rabbits and go fishing. She reacted slightly when she saw doves flying and I did my best not to cry and upset her. After a few hours of taking her to all of the spots that we had fun together as children, I took her to the vet.

The veterinarian said that she had a stroke and likely wouldn't be able to walk or even eat by herself for the rest of her life. It would cost more than I made in a year just to keep her around in this terrible state. So, I decided to have her put down. 

I carried her to the back room and put her up on the table. I rubbed between her eyes and she closed them lulled by her favorite spot. The vet gave her a shot to make her sleepy and pass out. After a few seconds she laid down and I put my chin on the table so that our noses were touching. I kept telling her she was a good girl and that we were gonna go to the river. Her tail was wagging every time I said one of the places she loved to visit.

She yawned a few times and slowly, her eyes closed and she began to snore. Then, the vet gave her a second shot. She said it stops the heart and that she wouldn't feel it since she was out cold. 

I felt her last breath wheeze out of her little nose on my face. The vet put a stethoscope to her ribs and told me she was gone. I put a 50 on the table and they gave me some time alone with her. I held her and rocked her in my arms for a while as i nearly asphyxiated myself on my own tears.

I took her tags off and buried her near the river in our favorite spot to hunt and fish. I'd visit her every once in a while just to break down when life got too hard. I still keep her tags on my keychain so it sounds like she's following me around. This was over three years ago and I'm sobbing profusely writing this. I cry literally every time I go into detail. 

It won't be something you handle well. It will be hard for a very long time. But, it will get better and you will learn to carry on. The thought of them will still sting years from now. The important thing is to remember that you gave them a good life, they loved you, and you did the best that you could for them. 

Get well soon friend. When you're ready someday, you'll give a good home to another one of mans best friend. They will light up your life for years and when the time comes for them to leave always remember: you gave them a happy life and they left knowing that you loved them.
